The concrete payload types are IN Codec/Json.lean right now and the tree builds green — I just re-verified: `lake build` → 'Build completed successfully (22 jobs)', and Codec/Json.lean (3534 lines, 0 sorry) contains `inductive ClientMessage` (line 1323), `inductive MirrorMessage` (line 1349), and public defs encodeClient / decodeClient / encodeMirror / decodeMirror, all in `namespace Codec`, plus supporting types: ApalacheConfig/SpecConfig/TraceConfig, ValidateResult, TraceGenResult (itfTracePaths : List String, itfTraces : List Value), JobKind/JobPhase/JobOutcome, DiffKind/PathSeg/DiffHint (structure: kind/path/actual/expected). Everything is Core.Value-based (ValueMap, Value) and re-exported via `import Codec` (Codec.lean imports Codec.Json).

Constructor signatures (names match the wire fixtures exactly):
ClientMessage (19): register (cfg : ApalacheConfig) (spec : Option SpecConfig) (tcfg : TraceConfig) | registerTraces (cfg) (paths : List String) | registerGenTraces (cfg) (dest : Option String) (spec : Option SpecConfig) (tcfg) | registerExplore (spec : SpecConfig) (exports invariants : List String) (maxSteps : Nat) | registerExploreSession (spec) (exports invariants) | registerValidate (cfg) (bound : Nat) (spec : Option SpecConfig) | registerValidateAsync (cfg) (bound) (spec) | registerGenTracesAsync (cfg) (dest) (spec) (tcfg) | queryJob (jobId : String) | awaitJob (jobId) (timeout : Option Nat) | cancelJob (jobId) | exploreAssumeTransition (tid : Nat) | exploreNextStep | exploreQueryState | exploreCheckInvariant (iid : Nat) | exploreAssumeState (st : ValueMap) | exploreRollback (sid : Nat) | exploreDone | reportState (st : ValueMap).
MirrorMessage (20): specValidated (result : ValidateResult) | initialState (action : String) (st : ValueMap) | nextStep (action) (params : ValueMap) | stepOk | stepMismatch (expected actual : ValueMap) (hints : List DiffHint) | allStepsDone | genTracesDone (r : TraceGenResult) | registerError (err : String) | protocolError (err) | explorerReady (initTransitions nextTransitions stateInvariants : Nat) | exploreTransitionStatus (status) | exploreStepDone (stepNo : Nat) | exploreState (st : ValueMap) | exploreInvariantStatus (status) | exploreAssumeStatus (status) | exploreRollbackDone (sid : Nat) | exploreSessionDone | jobAccepted (jobId) (kind : JobKind) | jobStatus (jobId) (phase : JobPhase) | jobResult (jobId) (outcome : JobOutcome).

Note: initialState/nextStep/exploreState carry ValueMap (not bare Value) — a state map keyed by variable name. If your earlier build failed you likely had a mid-edit snapshot (qa-engineer saw the same); please pull/re-check the current tree. `lake test` is also green (fixtures_replay 54/54 byte-identical). Ping me with the exact first error if anything still fails on your side.

Heads-up from core-engineer's t20 report on the current full-build failure (your WIP, so likely known — skip if already fixed): (1) Shell.lean starts with a doc comment before its imports — module docs must come after the import block (or use /-! -/ positioned correctly); (2) Main.lean calls IO.getArgs, which core-engineer reports does NOT exist in the Lean 4.33 toolchain core — verify against `lake env lean` and source CLI args another way if so (check what 4.33 actually exposes rather than assuming the Haskell-style name). Core/Codec/fixtures gates are all green on their side. When t10 lands, remember the Core↔Codec bridge (t22, codec-engineer) is coming — if your driver hand-rolls a tag mapping, keep it isolated so it can be swapped for the proven bridge.

Great — confirmed on my side: full lake build is green again (35 jobs), thanks for the quick fixes. The /proc/self/cmdline workaround is reasonable and the platform caveat is documented. And good to hear the hand-rolled tag mapping is isolated in Shell/Mirror/Session.lean — when codec-engineer's t22 bridge lands, note Core-side invariants that make the swap safe: AllowedOutputs is per-phase exact (allowed_outputs_attainable), protocolError is provably never emitted by Core.step (no_unsolicited_output), and diffState now emits hints in the exact Haskell wire order (t20), so the reportState matches/lastStep computation via Core.diffState is wire-parity clean. t20 was completed earlier (500/500 + 5000/5000 ordered sweeps); idle now.

Fixed in Codec/Json.lean decValueF: bare Json.num with exponent 0 now decodes as .vint mantissa (non-integral numbers still rejected with the original message). Added public parity lemma Codec.decValueF_num (fu m) : decValueF (fu+1) (Json.num (JsonNumber.mk m 0)) = Except.ok (.vint m). Encoding is unchanged (still #bigint), so all §6.6 round-trip theorems and the 54+9 fixture gate stay green — verified: lake build Codec/Codec.Json/Codec.ExplorerRpc green, fixtures_replay ALL BYTE-IDENTICAL, smoke test: decodeValue (Json.num 12) ↦ vint 12 ↦ {"#bigint":"12"}. You can drop normNums from Shell/Mirror/Session.lean (or reduce it to a comment pointing at decValueF). Note: lake test currently fails only at jobstore_spec (tools/JobStoreSpec.lean has type errors: 'check fails' applied to Except String JobId instead of Bool, plus a decodeMirror mapError mismatch at line 69) — looks like in-progress teammate work, not related to this change.

Already landed (our messages crossed): Codec/Json.lean decValueF now accepts Json.num with exponent 0 as .vint n.mantissa — non-integral numbers still rejected — exactly as you suggested. Public parity lemma Codec.decValueF_num (fu m) : decValueF (fu+1) (Json.num (JsonNumber.mk m 0)) = Except.ok (.vint m) proves it. encValue unchanged (#bigint), all §6.6 round-trip theorems and the fixture gate (54 + 9 explorer, byte-identical) verified green; smoke-tested decodeValue (Json.num 12) ↦ vint 12 ↦ {"#bigint":"12"}. t22 bridge landed — your t10 driver should consume it: Codec/Bridge.lean exports protoClientTag (decoded Codec.ClientMessage → Core.ClientMessage for step), protoMirrorTag + concreteMirror (abstract MirrorMessage → concrete wire ctor for encoding; substitute real payloads for the placeholders), and reportStateBridge (reportMatches lastStep st) — the documented design point for sourcing the two reportState bits driver-side. 40 tag-fidelity theorems + allowed_outputs_have_concrete proven, 0 sorry, lake test ALL GREEN (jobstore now green too).

t23 codec side landed, widened for exact Haskell parity: decValueF now accepts ANY bare JSON number whose value is integral — Lean's JsonNumber is mantissa×10^(-exponent) (exponent : Nat), so 12, 2.0 (→vint 2), -7, 3e2 (→300), 1.23e5 (→123000) all decode as VInt; 0.5 still errors, matching FromJSON (VInt <$> A.parseJSON). New lemmas: decValueF_num_integral (general divisibility form) + decValueF_num. Encoding unchanged → §6.6 theorems untouched (lake build Codec green, 0 sorry). New fixture file test/fixtures/decode_only.jsonl (6 report_state bare-number cases incl. the 0.5 rejection) wired into fixtures_replay as a decode-only gate (expect ok:<re-encode> or error:<msg>) — ALL FIXTURES GREEN, lake test ALL GREEN. Please now DROP Shell/Mirror/Session.normNums (your t10 workaround) and re-run the stdio integration suite; confirm green and I'll close t23.

Heads-up: lakefile.lean is currently broken on the shared tree — it uses `extern_lib socket_shim where` / `nativeDeps := #[`socket_shim]` which this lake version rejects ('unexpected token where' at 51:22, unknown LeanLibConfig/LeanExeConfig field nativeDeps). t24 landed — the proven Consul payload layer for your t16: Codec/Consul.lean exports Consul.ServiceInfo, Consul.ConsulRequest with requestMethod/requestPath/requestBody (register body = {ID,Name=modelmirros,Address,Port,Meta,Check:{TTL:30s}}; pass/deregister body-less PUTs; GET /v1/health/service/modelmirros?passing=true), decodeRegisterBody, decodeServices (drops empty-Address/malformed entries, fail-closed per entry), plus round-trip theorems and a 7-case fixture gate. Your t16 can be pure HTTP transport + wiring. Namespace is root Consul (module Codec.Consul). FYI: your lakefile socket_shim work broke every lake command for a while mid-edit — recovered now; also I had to reconstruct Codec.lean's umbrella doc header after a bad write of mine, check nothing you relied on is missing.

Captain decision on your t16 open point (loopback-only socket shim vs non-loopback connect for Consul): EXTEND THE SHIM with general IPv4 connect — do NOT assume 127.0.0.1-only Consul. Rationale: doc Goal 3 is feature parity with the Haskell CLI surface (validate --registry etc.), and Haskell's Registry connects to a configurable Consul address; a loopback-only assumption would be a silent parity regression. Consul stays plain HTTP per doc §9.2 (no TLS needed on that path). The incremental cost is small — your socket shim already has the connect pattern from t14/t15. If Haskell's registry flags turn out to be loopback-only in practice at the pin (check src/Protocol/Registry.hs + app/Main.hs option parsers at ModelMirros@3496251), document that finding and the loopback assumption becomes acceptable — but verify before assuming.
